views.title: State and trust boundaries
views.question: Where can plaintext, keys and the sole authoritative copy exist?

nodes.label:
Microservice / CLI
Authorized plaintext in use
L1 is optional memory only

Native controller replicas
Authenticated tenant + task
Plaintext validation / sealing

Independent key broker
KEKs + signing authority
Separate permit generation

Local derived views
Rebuildable search / plots
Explicit export disclosure

Selected source backend
PostgreSQL or local bare Git
Ciphertext + CAS head

Independent authority DB
Grants, epochs, exact prepares
Pending / accepted frontiers

WAL / base backup / replica
Encrypted durable copies
Retained keys required

Source outbox + receipts
Encrypted durable pending work
Part of source transaction

Isolated projection gateway
Permit unwrap + SSH only
No source DB or domain key

Optional remote Git
Verified encrypted projection
Never an active second writer

views.notes: Every source and authority has its own storage/backup owner. Controller scratch must be protected and nonswappable. Gateway scratch holds ciphertext and permit plaintext only. Native reference uses two stateless controllers; local Git requires one fenced writer. Operational endpoints use the same private mTLS app.

views.title: Write and acknowledgment
views.question: What must be durable before a caller receives success?

nodes.label:
1. Authenticated request
Tenant / subject / grant / task
Stable operation ID

2. Current authority check
Policy + epoch + exact frontier
Reauthorize cached reads

3. Validate and seal
Fresh DEK + nonce; pinned signer
Explicit envelope context

4. Durable exact prepare
Authority retains candidate
Uncertainty blocks new work

5. Source acceptance CAS
Objects + head + receipt + outbox
One database/Git transaction

6. Authority acknowledgment
Read back accepted exact root
Clear matching pending work

7. Local durable receipt
Client observes new generation
Invalidate stale memory entries

8. Optional remote delivery
Separate retained requirement
Local receipt remains durable

9. Workload completion
All originally required targets
Must be independently verified

views.notes: PostgreSQL synchronous mode requires remote_apply and a configured synchronous standby. Local Git fsyncs objects and the root transition under an inherited process lock. An unknown commit is recovered by exact operation ID. No remote-required completion is inferred from an empty queue.

views.title: Branches and reviewed derivation
views.question: Which gates separate a branch, disclosed child history and semantic adoption?

nodes.label:
1. Pin source frontier
Ordered revision parents
Expected heads + epoch

2a. Branch / tag
Reference existing revision
Source remains authoritative

2b. Fork / split candidate
Explicit selected disclosure
Independent child scope + keys

3. Review exact candidate
Source and child grants current
Parent adoption is explicit

4. Prepare exact group
Retain project/export obligations
Freeze all affected scopes

5. Apply / verify batches
Stable IDs; byte-identical retries
No partial public group frontier

6. Atomic authority publication
All group receipts present
Advance complete frontiers

7. Reviewed reconciliation
Pinned head(s), ordered parents
No rewrite of source journals

8. Separate remote verification
Each accepted intent retained
Adoption is not replication

views.notes: Fork/split creates selected child histories under separately provisioned scopes. The caller cannot acquire parent or sibling visibility from a child name. Group recovery preserves prepared bytes even if current scheduling changes. Ordinary branch publication does not require a derivation group.

views.title: Projection timing and custody
views.question: When may remote history lag, and what proves delivery?

nodes.label:
1. Accepted encrypted intent
Destination, permit key and policy
Retained with original receipt

2. Explicit scheduling
Manual / interval / batch / required
Disabled retains accepted work

3. Persist exact preparation
Archive + Git OID + expected head
Signed permit; no remote call yet

4. Persist attempt / backoff
State becomes unknown
Before first transport effect

5. Isolated gateway
Current caller + writer policy
Permit-only unwrap; verify archive

6. SSH expected-head update
Parent-preserving candidate
Divergence blocks publication

7. Independent fresh fetch
Exact commit / tree / blob
Recheck advertised ref

8. Retain verified receipt
Advance observed watermark
Remove only matching queue item

9. Original target-set gate
Missing evidence stays incomplete
Timer never proves durability

views.notes: Default policy is disabled. Configured defaults: 60 s interval, batch 8, lag budget 3600 s, retry 1 to 60 s, 5 attempts; actual accepted targets and key generation are immutable intent data. Entry/byte/lag pressure refuses affected writes. Full snapshots retain history and amplify storage; limits are not an incremental format.

views.title: Failure and recovery boundaries
views.question: Which durable evidence permits recovery, and where must work stop?

nodes.label:
Failure or uncertain reply
Process / network / provider loss
Keep operation ID and frontier

Source transaction unknown
Resolve exact retained batch
Never guess absence

Authority pending prepare
Verify committed candidate
Then acknowledge or resume

Primary or node loss
Fence old primary independently
Promote verified replica

New authority epoch
Reject every stale controller
Reconcile accepted frontier

Key or policy outage
Block decrypt / write / publication
Do not serve cached plaintext

Remote reply lost / diverged
Reuse exact bytes and read back
Divergence needs reviewed repair

Backup / PITR restore
Inactive target; retained keys
Verify counts, signatures, roots

Resume only after verification
Reconcile remote effects + grants
No revived revoked access

views.notes: Physical drill uses a killed primary, synchronous replica promotion and separate PITR from verified base backup plus archived WAL. Recovery times are local observations. Operator owns old-primary fencing, encrypted volumes, backup retention and restore trust. A live replica is not an independent backup.

views.title: Migration and rollback
views.question: What permits a routing change without losing accepted history?

nodes.label:
1. Explicit reviewed plan
Exact source / destination / scope
Permissions, keys, backup proof

2. Pin snapshot + watermark
Complete approved history
Retain exact original Git objects

3. Encrypted backfill
Immutable IDs + signatures
Idempotent exact-byte copies

4. Catch up committed deltas
Refs, receipts, mappings, grants
No silent second writable master

5. Fence and drain
Resolve pending source/outbox
Final complete comparison

6. Exact cutover prepare
Atomic backend + epoch change
Old epoch immediately denied

7. Verify target canary
New writes / read / branch / recovery
Retain old source and keys

8. Rollback after new writes
Fence target; reverse catch-up
Include every new accepted effect

9. Verified reverse frontier
Same integrity / permission gate
New epoch, then routing switch

views.notes: Git and PostgreSQL preserve the canonical native history sidecar. Exact original Git objects and OIDs are retained by the archive profile, not rewritten to represent new exports. Unsupported reverse representations block rollback. Retention cleanup, private migration and pilot enrollment require separate approval.
